papers.title: Geometry in Active Learning for Binary and Multi-class Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: We propose an active learning approach to image segmentation that exploits geometric priors to speed up and streamline the annotation process. It can be applied for both background-foreground and multi-class segmentation tasks in 2D images and 3D image volumes. Our approach combines geometric smoothness priors in the image space with more traditional uncertainty measures to estimate which pixels or voxels are the most informative, and thus should to be annotated next. For multi-class settings, we additionally introduce two novel criteria for uncertainty. In the 3D case, we use the resulting uncertainty measure to select voxels lying on a planar patch, which makes batch annotation much more convenient for the end user compared to the setting where voxels are randomly distributed in a volume. The planar patch is found using a branch-and-bound algorithm that looks for a 2D patch in a 3D volume where the most informative instances are located. We evaluate our approach on Electron Microscopy and Magnetic Resonance image volumes, as well as on regular images of horses and faces. We demonstrate a substantial performance increase over other approaches thanks to the use of geometric priors.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文聚焦于图像分割中的主动学习，与有限元仿真替代模型或生物力学设计方向无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address surrogate modeling, finite element analysis, or any form of computational mechanics; it focuses solely on active learning for image segmentation with geometric priors.

summary_zh.motivation: 加速图像分割的标注过程
summary_zh.method: 利用几何平滑先验与不确定性度量的主动学习
summary_zh.result: 在多种2D/3D图像数据上显著提升分割性能
summary_zh.validation: 在电子显微镜和磁共振图像上评估

summary_en.motivation: To speed up annotation for image segmentation by selecting the most informative pixels or voxels.
summary_en.method: Combines geometric smoothness priors with uncertainty measures, and uses branch-and-bound to find planar patches for batch annotation in 3D.
summary_en.result: Achieves substantial performance gains over other active learning approaches on EM, MRI, and natural images.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated on Electron Microscopy and Magnetic Resonance image volumes, as well as standard image datasets.

papers.title: Numerical analysis of heat transfer during multi-layer selective laser melting of AlSi10Mg
papers.first_author_affiliation: Chongqing Institute of Green and Intelligent Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Chongqing 400714, China

corresponding_authors.name: Xueping Ding
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Chongqing Institute of Green and Intelligent Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Chongqing 400714, China

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究SLM过程中的热传递数值模拟，未涉及生物医学植入物设计或力学测试。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on thermal simulation of SLM for AlSi10Mg, with no biomedical implant context, no pore structure design, no mechanical testing, no stress shielding analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究多层选区激光熔化过程中的热传递行为。
summary_zh.method: 建立多层SLM热传递数值模型，分析激光参数对温度场的影响。
summary_zh.result: 揭示了多层沉积过程中的热循环特征。
summary_zh.validation: 与文献中的实验温度数据对比验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the heat transfer behavior during multi-layer selective laser melting process.
summary_en.method: A numerical model for heat transfer in multi-layer SLM was developed to analyze the effect of laser parameters on temperature field.
summary_en.result: The thermal cycling characteristics during multi-layer deposition were revealed.
summary_en.validation: The model was validated by comparing with experimental temperature data from literature.

papers.title: Noise production in ceramic-on-ceramic total hip arthroplasty is associated with lower patient satisfaction and hip scores
papers.first_author_affiliation: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, 1345 Govan Road, Glasgow G51 4TF, UK

corresponding_authors.name: Ian W. Kennedy
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, 1345 Govan Road, Glasgow G51 4TF, UK

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究陶瓷对陶瓷全髋关节置换术中的噪音问题与患者满意度，未涉及生物力学建模或植入物设计。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical outcomes study on noise after THA; it does not include FEA, stress/strain quantification, micromotion analysis, or implant design comparison.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究陶瓷对陶瓷全髋关节置换术后噪音产生与患者满意度和髋关节评分的关联。
summary_zh.method: 对接受陶瓷对陶瓷全髋置换的患者进行问卷调查和临床评估。
summary_zh.result: 术后噪音与较低的患者满意度和髋关节评分显著相关。
summary_zh.validation: 基于临床随访数据的统计分析。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the association between noise generation after ceramic-on-ceramic total hip arthroplasty and patient-reported outcomes.
summary_en.method: Clinical evaluation and questionnaires were administered to patients who underwent ceramic-on-ceramic THA, focusing on the presence and impact of noise.
summary_en.result: Noise production was significantly associated with lower patient satisfaction and hip scores.
summary_en.validation: Statistical analysis of clinical follow-up data with validated outcome measures.
